correctness.rationale: Checked the actual Baronti–Bertella H_2 definition, normalization and lambda-reduction, and Balestro–Martini–Teixeira classification y=±Rx for all unit isosceles orthogonal partners in symmetric planes. Setting lambda=tan theta gives ratio 1/||Q_theta x||; maximizing over unit x is the norm of Q_{-theta}, equal to Q_theta by axis reflection. For regular 4n-gon with circumradius sec a, support normals at 2a lattice, each vertex has rotated norm cos(dist(a+theta,2aZ))/cos a <=sec a; theta=a reaches the maximum. Includes n=1 square and n=2 octagon, no unjustified extension to other polygons.
residual_risks: No assertion for arbitrary centrally symmetric polygons or nonsymmetric planes.

value.rationale: The identity converts a nonlinear isosceles-orthogonality extremal problem on an entire natural symmetry class of normed planes into a computable Euclidean-rotation operator-norm invariant. Exact secant law across all affine regular 4n-gons is a motivated natural family, not an isolated arbitrary octagon value.

final_claim: For every real symmetric Minkowski plane with coordinate axes, H_2 equals sup_{0<=theta<=pi/4} ||Q_theta||, and for every affine regular 4n-gonal plane equals sec(pi/(4n)).
